title: Bussa's Rebellion, Barbados
summary: On Easter Sunday night, 14 April 1816, enslaved people in St Philip parish, Barbados, burned cane fields to signal a planned island-wide uprising, named for the African-born leader Bussa. More than seventy estates were affected before militia and British troops crushed it under martial law; by September 144 people had been executed and 170 deported.

uncertainty.note: Start is the night of Easter Sunday, 14 April 1816; martial law was declared 15 April and lasted eighty days (BlackPast). The leaders had planned to rise on 17 April (CARICOM).

as_recorded.value: The rebellion started on Easter Sunday night April 14, 1816

where.historical_name: St Philip parish, Colony of Barbados, British Empire

importance.justification: Largest slave revolt in Barbados and the first of three major late revolts in the British West Indies before emancipation.

sources.title: Two hundred years since the heroic Barbados slave rebellion
